subject: SLO exception request — batch ingestion API (Sierra Strata)
messages:
From: Elena Cruz <elena@sierrastrata.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.com
Cc: procure@sierrastrata.com
Date: Thu, 21 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLO exception request for batch ingestion API

Hi Aditya —

Thanks for the demo last week. We’re close to legal/ops alignment, but we hit a blocker: our on-prem data router occasionally delays large batches for up to 45 minutes during nightly reconciliation windows. That makes meeting Redwood’s standard 99.95% uptime for the batch ingestion endpoint impractical for our initial rollout.

Ask: Can Redwood accept a scoped SLO exception for the batch ingestion API in our non-prod and pilot regions to 99.5% uptime for the first 12 months, with a capped service-credit remedy (max 20% of monthly invoice) instead of unlimited proportional credits? Legal asked for something in writing — attached is our short request and a draft of the affected endpoint list.

We’re on a tight timeline for a June 15 launch — happy to jump on a quick call if that helps.

Thanks,
Elena Cruz
Head of Platform Ops
Sierra Strata

Aditya —

I reviewed the attachment and put inline notes on two items:
- Limit exception to pilot regions only (not global prod).
- Cap service credits at 20% of monthly bill and add a 30-day cure window before credits apply.

Questions for Deal Desk: do we have precedent for capped credits at 20% for pilot exceptions? Finance flagged that a lower cap reduces our collection risk. Also, confirm whether we can require they run with our monitoring agents in those pilot regions as a condition.

If we can get a quick sign-off from Markus or Stephanie today, I’ll prepare the SLA exhibit and get legal to run the wording.

From: markus_klein@redwood.com

Cc: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 22 May 2026 08:09:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: SLO exception request for batch ingestion API — Sierra Strata (DEAL-7891)

TL;DR: I’m comfortable approving a constrained exception if we protect Redwood’s downside. Proposed executive terms:
- Scoped exception: 99.5% uptime for batch ingestion API, pilot regions only, 12 months.
- Remedy: capped service credit at 20% of monthly bill per month, applied only after a 30-day cure window.
- Condition: Sierra Strata must install Redwood monitoring agents and participate in joint incident drills for the pilot.
- Discount request: they asked for a 10% platform discount tied to this SLA — I recommend passing on the discount, but we can offer a one-time onboarding credit up to $5k instead.

I’ve attached redlines (redlines_sla_v2.docx). Please escalate to Stephanie for final sign-off (exec approval needed for any deviation from standard remedies).

— Markus

To: markus_klein@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 24 May 2026 09:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLO exception request — approval (DEAL-7891)

Thanks for the context. I approve the exception under the conditions Markus outlined. Final approval notes:
- Approve scoped SLO exception: 99.5% uptime for batch ingestion API, pilot regions only, 12 months.
- Approve capped remedy: 20% monthly cap, after 30-day cure window.
- No ongoing platform discount; approve $5,000 one-time onboarding credit.
- Require installation of Redwood monitoring agents and quarterly joint drills for duration of exception.

Aditya — please proceed to get updated SLA exhibit into DocuSign and share link with Elena. Legal to review final draft but marketing/sales may proceed with the terms.

Stephanie
